Edmund Spenser, The Faerie Queene.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/edmund-spenser/the-faerie-queene

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Edmund Spenser, the author and the writer of the preface, died 1599.

First publication of the text used: 1596 (SE colophon: 'The Faerie Queene was published in 1596 by Edmund Spenser. This ebook was transcribed and produced for Standard Ebooks by Emma Sweeney, and is based on digital scans from the Internet Archive. The cover page is adapted from The Ermine Portrait of Elizabeth I of England, a painting completed in 1585 by Sir William Segar. The cover and title pages feature the League Spartan and Sorts Mill Goudy typefaces created in 2014 and 2009 by The League of Moveable Type. The first edition of this ebook was released on December 22, 2022, 7:23 a.m. You can check for updates to this ebook, view its revision history, or download it for different ereading systems at standardebooks.org/ebooks/edmund-spenser/the-faerie-queene. The volunteer-driven Standard Ebooks project relies on readers like you to submit typos, corrections, and other improvements. Anyone can contribute at standardebooks.org.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the Standard Ebooks rights statement says the text is in the US public domain, and the text was first published in 1596, before 1931, so it is public domain there.
- Country of origin: every person named above died in 1925 or earlier, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less. The last to die did so in 1599, so this holds by 1 January 1700.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
